title.en: The Rainbow: the poem in brief

text.en: The poet compares boats, ships and bridges to the rainbow in the sky.

The first stanza says boats sail on rivers and ships on seas, but the clouds that sail across the sky are prettier than both.
The second stanza says bridges on rivers are pretty, but the bow in the sky that goes over the trees and makes a road from earth to sky is prettier.
The poet likes the rainbow best, because it is natural and reaches the heavens.
The word 'bow' here means a curved arch, a rainbow, not a bow and arrow.
The word 'these' refers to boats and ships in stanza one and to river bridges in stanza two.
New words are overtops, bridges and bow.

requiredIdeas.en: The poet likes the rainbow more

The rainbow is a road between earth and sky.
